# @ic-reactor/core

> How to call Internet Computer canisters with a module `candid-core-cli gen`
> generated from a `.did`, a client from `@ic-reactor/core`, and TanStack
> Query. The client applies the rules a hand-written integration must get
> right; this guide names the call for each.

Applies to `@ic-reactor/core` 4.0.0-beta.6.

## Imports

```ts
import { createClient, formatUnits, isReactorError, parseUnits } from "@ic-reactor/core"
import { ReactorProvider, useAuth, useClient } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { isPrincipal, principal, type Principal } from "@candid-core/schema"
import { skipToken, useMutation, useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { actor, type Actor } from "./generated/icrc1"
```

One import path per name: Candid values only from `@candid-core/schema`,
`skipToken` and the hooks only from TanStack Query.

`@ic-reactor/core` and `@ic-reactor/react` are ES modules only. A Node
project needs `"type": "module"` in its `package.json`
(`npm pkg set type=module`), or a bundler; `npx tsx` with
top-level `await` fails in a CommonJS package. Under TypeScript's
`moduleResolution: "nodenext"`, import local files with their `.js`
extension (`./generated/icrc1.js`).

The generated module (from `candid-core-cli gen` or `@ic-reactor/vite-plugin`;
do not edit it) exports a type and schema per Candid type, the service schema
`actor`, and `type Actor`.

## Setup

```ts
// src/ledger.ts
import { createClient } from "@ic-reactor/core"
import { actor, type Actor } from "./generated/icrc1"

export const client = createClient({ network: "ic", identity: "anonymous" })
export const ledger = client.canister<Actor>(actor, { id: "ryjl3-tyaaa-aaaaa-aaaba-cai" })
```

`client.canister()` returns the same object each time: safe in render.

With React, install `@tanstack/query-core` at the exact version your
`@tanstack/react-query` depends on (`npm view @tanstack/react-query@<version>
dependencies`), and check that `npm ls @tanstack/query-core` shows one copy.
With two copies, core and the hooks each have their own `skipToken`:
`client.queryOptions()` throws a `TypeError` for the hooks' one, and in
development `ReactorProvider` throws when it is handed such a client.

`network` and the root key:

- `"ic"`: mainnet (`https://icp-api.io`) and its built-in root key.
- `"local"`: icp-cli's local network, `http://127.0.0.1:8000`; its root key
  is fetched. A dfx replica is `{ host: "http://127.0.0.1:4943" }`.
- `{ host, rootKey }`: any other replica. A given `rootKey` is used, never
  fetched; without one, it is fetched only from a local `host` (`localhost`,
  `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). Never fetch one from any other host.
- `"env"`: the page's network. Canisters can be named, `{ name: "backend" }`,
  from the `ic_env` cookie, believed only on a local replica or with
  `allowEnvConfig: true`. A server has no cookie: use `{ id }` there.
  `"env"` is for `localhost` pages: a LAN or Tailscale address, a LAN name
  with no dot, `*.local`, `*.test`, `*.internal`, `*.ts.net`, a tunnel or a
  dev container routes to its own origin (never mainnet) but does not
  believe the cookie or take a root key.
  `allowEnvConfig: true` throws on `ic0.app`, `*.app.github.dev` and
  `*.gitpod.io` pages (not public suffixes: any sibling site can set the
  cookie), and never takes the cookie's root key for a mainnet host.
  `client.canisterId({ name })` says, without a call, what a name resolves
  to: `{ ok: true, id }`, or `{ ok: false, reason, message }` with `reason`
  `"no_browser"`, `"untrusted_host"` or `"absent"`, and the resolver's reason
  text, which a call's error includes after the method and target.
- Without the Vite plugin (Next.js, webpack, esbuild) there is no cookie and no
  `/api` proxy, so `"env"` and `{ name }` do not work on a local network. Use
  `network: "local"` with `{ id }` from a build-time variable
  (`NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_ID`, written from
  `icp canister status -e local -i backend` into
  `.env.development.local`, which only `next dev` reads).

Deploying to mainnet (`icp deploy -e ic`): with `"env"`, a canister's own
`<id>.icp0.io` (or `<id>.raw.icp0.io`) page believes its cookie's canister
ids (a public suffix: no sibling can set it), never its root key. On
`<id>.ic0.app` and custom domains `{ name }` does not resolve. For a page that
works everywhere, name canisters `{ id: import.meta.env.VITE_BACKEND_ID }`,
with the local id in `.env.development` and the mainnet id
(`icp canister status backend -e ic -i`) in `.env.production`. Never set
`allowEnvConfig: true` on `ic0.app`; on a custom domain only when every
subdomain is yours.

`createClient` throws a `TypeError` for an option it does not have (`host`
goes inside `network`), an `allowEnvConfig` or `fetchRootKey` that is not a
boolean (environment text: `=== "true"`), and a `rootKey` that is not 133
bytes in a `Uint8Array` (decode hex first).

Who calls (exactly one):

- `identity`: a fixed `Identity` (scripts, servers, tests), or `"anonymous"`,
  read-only: every update is refused before sending. A
  `new AnonymousIdentity()` signs writes, so map one you are handed:
  `identity: id && !id.getPrincipal().isAnonymous() ? id : "anonymous"`.
- `auth: (network) => new AuthClient(network)` (`@icp-sdk/auth/client`):
  users sign in and out. The factory runs once, in a browser only; if it
  throws (blocked `localStorage`), the client stays anonymous, public reads
  still work, and `signIn()` rejects with that error. `network`
  is `{ agentOptions, identityProvider? }`: the client's host and root key
  (and its `fetch`, when you gave one), and the Internet Identity to sign in
  with (the `ic_env` cookie's, or icp-cli's built-in one for a local host). Absent on a mainnet client, it
  means mainnet's. Absent on any other network (a project that deploys its
  own `internet_identity`, `"env"` on a local page with no
  `INTERNET_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` in the cookie, a replica with its own root
  key), sign-in cannot work, and a factory that reads
  `network.identityProvider`, as `new AuthClient(network)` does, gets a
  warning once in development. Name the provider there, which never warns:
  `(network) => new AuthClient({ ...network, identityProvider: { authorizeUrl, canisterId } })`.
  A spread that adds other options, `{ ...network, derivationOrigin }`, reads no
  provider and gets no warning, so name one there too.
  `() => new AuthClient()` ignores `network`, so it suits mainnet only.

Who is calling, and may they write:

| Question               | Answer                                                                    |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| the caller's principal | `useAuth().principal`, `client.caller()` (`"2vxsx-fae"` unless signed in) |
| may a write be sent    | `useAuth().status === "signed-in"`; the client refuses the rest itself    |
| when did it change     | `useAuth()` re-renders; `client.subscribe(fn)`                            |

`"signed-in"` may be a read-only session (Internet Identity can scope one to
queries, and the network refuses its updates); nothing tells the two apart
yet. A session ends by the clock: `useAuth()` re-renders with `"expired"` at
`expiresAt` (ms since the epoch, present while signed in), with no user
activity.

The client keeps one agent per principal: a call goes out as the principal
current when it was made, or not at all.

One client per browser tab, or per request on a server. In React,
`<ReactorProvider client={() => createClient(...)}>` builds it once per
mounted tree and disposes it on unmount; a module-scope client passed as
`client={() => client}` is borrowed, never disposed. A client made outside a
provider, or kept across its unmount, is the app's to release with
`client.dispose()` (calling it again does nothing; later calls reject
`cancelled`, code `client_disposed`, and send nothing); one that lives as long
as the page needs none. Inside, `useClient()`
returns a view of it for the caller the render shows (anonymous while
hydrating): a new object after each sign-in, switch or sign-out, the same one
while the caller stays, whose `mutationOptions` send only as that caller (a
write pressed before a switch reaches the render is refused `cancelled`,
`caller_changed`, and sends nothing). `useAuth()` returns
`{ status, principal, expiresAt?, signIn, signOut }`, `"anonymous"` on a server and in a
hydrating page's first render.

An app that already uses TanStack Query keeps one `QueryClient` per tree,
the client's: run its own queries (REST too) under `ReactorProvider`, on
`client.queryClient`. An error that is not a `ReactorError` is retried there
as TanStack Query retries it (up to 3 times in a browser), and
`client.dispose()` clears those queries too. A nested `QueryClientProvider` of
the app's still has its reads invalidated by a write that ran on it, but a
server render dehydrates `client.queryClient`.

Any other sign-in that hands over an `Identity` (a delegation, or a key)
becomes an `AuthLike`. A wallet that signs each call itself (ICRC-25 and
ICRC-49: OISY, Plug, NFID accounts) is not one: keep the client anonymous for
reads, send the wallet's writes with `SignerAgent` from `@icp-sdk/signer`, and
then invalidate the reads yourself with
`client.queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: client.queryKey(canister) })`.
Such a write gets no `ReactorError` and no `mayHaveExecuted`.

```ts
// src/auth-like.ts
import type { AuthLike } from "@ic-reactor/core"
import type { Identity } from "@icp-sdk/core/agent"

export interface SignInSource {
  getIdentity(): Identity // anonymous while signed out
  isAuthenticated(): boolean
  login(): Promise<void>
  logout(): Promise<void>
  subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void
}

export function toAuthLike(source: SignInSource): AuthLike {
  const signedIn = () =>
    source.isAuthenticated() && !source.getIdentity().getPrincipal().isAnonymous()
  return {
    getPrincipal: () => (signedIn() ? source.getIdentity().getPrincipal() : undefined),
    getStatus: () => ({ state: signedIn() ? "signed-in" : "signed-out" }),
    getIdentity: async () => source.getIdentity(),
    subscribe: (listener) => source.subscribe(listener),
    signIn: () => source.login(),
    signOut: () => source.logout(),
  }
}
```

## Values

Methods use the generated types:

| Candid                                   | Value                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `nat`, `int`, `nat64`, `int64`           | `bigint` (never `number`)                      |
| `nat8`..`nat32`, `int8`..`int32`, floats | `number`                                       |
| `text`, `bool`                           | `string`, `boolean`                            |
| `principal`                              | `Principal`: branded principal text            |
| `blob` / `vec nat8`                      | `Uint8Array`                                   |
| `opt T`                                  | `T \| null` (the property is always present)   |
| `opt opt T`, `opt null`                  | `{ some: T \| null } \| null`, `{ some: null } \| null` |
| `vec T`                                  | `T[]`                                          |
| `record { a : T }`                       | `{ a: T }`, every field present                |
| `variant { A : T; B }`                   | `{ tag: "A"; value: T } \| { tag: "B" }`       |

Make principals from user input with `principal(text)`, which throws a
`TypeError` for invalid text: catch it and refuse the input. In render, test with `isPrincipal(text)` first.

Direct calls take the parameters `type Actor` lists; the builders below take
them as one value: nothing for none, the value for one, a tuple `[a, b]` for
more.

Token amounts are base units:

```ts
/// <reference lib="es2023.intl" />
import { formatUnits, parseUnits } from "@ic-reactor/core"

const units = parseUnits("1.5", 8) // 150000000n
const text = formatUnits(units, 8, { minFractionDigits: 8 }) // "1.50000000"
const local = new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { maximumFractionDigits: 8 }).format(
  text as Intl.StringNumericLiteral // the cast needs lib ES2023
)
```

`parseUnits` throws for text that is not a plain decimal (`"1e3"`, `"1,5"`),
a negative, or more significant fraction digits than `decimals`: refuse that
input. Trailing zeros, `"5."`, `".5"` and whitespace around the number are
accepted (`"1.500"` at 2 decimals is `150n`), so validate the field with
`parseUnits` itself, not another parser. A cap is the Candid
type's: a `nat64` field refuses 2^64 at encoding (`invalid_args`); an ICRC-1
`amount` is a `nat`, with none.

### Results

A method whose result is `variant { Ok : T; Err : E }` resolves with the `Ok`
value; `Err` rejects as kind `"canister_err"`, with the `Err` value in `err`
(typed on a query's or mutation's `error`).

## Reads

```tsx
import type { Principal } from "@candid-core/schema"
import { formatUnits } from "@ic-reactor/core"
import { useClient } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { skipToken, useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { actor, type Actor } from "./generated/icrc1"

export function Balance({ owner }: { owner: Principal | undefined }) {
  const client = useClient()
  const ledger = client.canister<Actor>(actor, { id: "ryjl3-tyaaa-aaaaa-aaaba-cai" })
  const balance = useQuery(
    client.queryOptions(ledger, "icrc1_balance_of", owner ? { owner, subaccount: null } : skipToken)
  )
  return <p>{balance.data === undefined ? "…" : formatUnits(balance.data, 8)}</p>
}
```

`skipToken` stands in for arguments not known yet;
arguments that do not encode make the read reject `invalid_args`.

Keys are `["ic-reactor", network, caller, canisterId, method, args]`, so one
principal's cached answer is never served to another: after a sign-in,
sign-out or switch, the new caller's key is empty (`data` is `undefined`)
until it loads, and a read made for the previous caller never lands in it.
Keep it so: build the options in render from that render's `useClient()`,
listing it in the dependencies of any `useMemo` or effect built from it
(React Compiler does), and add nothing that carries data across keys
(`placeholderData: keepPreviousData`, cross-key `initialData`).
`client.queryKey(ledger, method?, args?)` gives keys for the cache.

Reads retry transient failures (never on a server). Spread to add options:
`{ ...client.queryOptions(...), staleTime }`.

`queryOptions` with an update or oneway method of a generated `Actor` does
not compile (an `Actor` written by hand says no mode: it throws at run time).
An update that answers the same however often it runs (ckBTC's
`get_btc_address`) opts in with a fourth argument, `{ update: "idempotent" }`,
after the arguments (`undefined` when it takes none); a oneway never compiles.
Such a read is still an update, so a signed-out or `"anonymous"` client
refuses it (`unauthenticated`) and sends nothing. Read an ICRC-21 consent
message as the caller who will send the write: the message can depend on the
caller (the DFINITY ICRC-1 ledger names the sender as `From`).
A method TypeScript cannot tell is a read does not compile: a type parameter
(`M extends keyof A & string`), a union that may name an update
(`keyof Actor & string`), or any method of a `Canister<A>` with a generic `A`.
Give the type arguments,
`client.queryOptions<A, any>(canister, method, vars)`, which keeps the
run-time check and types the data `unknown`. The variables follow the same
rule, checked at run time: the value for one argument, a tuple for several,
`undefined` or `[]` for none (`[arg]` compiles but is refused
`invalid_args`). `mutationOptions`, `queryKey` and `resendOf` take
`<A, any>` the same way; for a generic `A` only `queryOptions` widens the
variables, so cast them for the other three.
The target `{ id, certified: true }` certifies `query` replies.

## Writes

```tsx
import { useClient } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { useMutation } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { actor, type Actor, type TransferArg } from "./generated/icrc1"

export function Send({ arg }: { arg: TransferArg }) {
  const client = useClient()
  const ledger = client.canister<Actor>(actor, { id: "ryjl3-tyaaa-aaaaa-aaaba-cai" })
  const transfer = useMutation(client.mutationOptions(ledger, "icrc1_transfer"))
  return <button disabled={transfer.isPending} onClick={() => transfer.mutate(arg)}>Send</button>
}
```

- The mutation invalidates the canister's reads, for every caller, after a
  success, a `canister_err` and a failure that may have executed. Nothing
  else is needed after an unknown outcome.
  A third argument, `{ invalidates: [canister, [canister, "method"]] }`,
  names the reads to invalidate instead (name the written canister too if
  its reads change); `[]`, none. To add an `onSettled`, call the client's
  from yours.
- A write that timed out (`timeoutMs`, below in Errors) whose request went
  out is `outcome_unknown`: never send it again blindly.
- Do not retry a write. `retry` is `false`; keep it. The client itself
  re-sends an update, at most twice, only after a failure proving the canister
  never got it (reject code 2, status 429); any other failure is final.
- A write is sent as the caller current when `mutate()` was called, or not at
  all. Held back by TanStack Query (offline, queued behind its `scope`, or
  retried) while the account changes, it is refused (`cancelled`,
  `caller_changed`, `mayHaveExecuted: false`) and nothing is sent. This holds
  with an `onMutate` of yours that replaces the client's, on
  `client.queryClient`. A mutation restored from a persister is always
  refused that way: call `mutate()` again. On another `QueryClient`, keep the
  client's `onMutate` (spread its result into yours; before TanStack Query
  5.89, pass it unwrapped). If nobody is signed in,
  the client refuses it (`unauthenticated`) before calling anything.
- Send the same write again after `mayHaveExecuted: true` only to a method
  that runs the same argument from the same sender at most once, such as an
  ICRC-1 transfer with `created_at_time` set (it answers `Duplicate`).
  Stamp that key from the IC's clock, `await client.time(ledger)` (a certified
  `bigint` of nanoseconds), not from `Date.now()`. That time moves about once
  a second, so give each transfer its own `memo` too.
  `client.resendOf(transfer.error, ledger, "icrc1_transfer", { dedupedBy: (arg) => arg.created_at_time })`
  is `undefined` unless that write's outcome is unknown, `dedupedBy` finds a
  key (not `null`) in its argument, the argument is unchanged since it was
  sent, the canister still resolves where the write went, and its sender is
  still the caller; then `again.send()` sends the same bytes to the same
  canister as that sender, and `transfer.mutate(again.arg)` sends the
  argument only as that same write, or rejects and sends nothing
  (`caller_changed`, `target_changed`, `arg_changed`). Such a refusal
  replaces the mutation's error, so `resendOf` offers nothing after it, and
  the first write's outcome is still unknown: read the state back, never
  ignore it as a plain `cancelled`. Never change an offered argument: build a new one for a new transfer. A method with no
  such key has no safe re-send: read the state back.
- For the exact bytes a write will send, such as an ICRC-21 consent
  request's `arg`, use `client.encode(ledger, "icrc1_transfer", arg)` (a
  `Uint8Array`, made by the call's own encoder; variables that do not encode
  throw `invalid_args`), never a second encoding of your own. An offered
  re-send carries the bytes it sent as `again.bytes`.
- A `canister_err` is a known outcome, so `resendOf` offers nothing after it.
  When the canister calls it temporary (an ICRC-1 `TemporarilyUnavailable`),
  send the same argument object again with `transfer.mutate(arg)`: with
  `created_at_time` set, that is the same bytes and the same key, answered
  `Duplicate` if an earlier attempt ran.
- To keep an offer in state, type it from the method:
  `NonNullable<ReturnType<typeof client.resendOf<Actor, "icrc1_transfer">>>`.
- Call update methods only from `useMutation` or directly, never from
  `useQuery`; call query methods from `useQuery` or directly.

## Errors

Every rejection is a `ReactorError`: test with `isReactorError(error)`, then
read `kind` and `mayHaveExecuted`. For a direct call, test with
`isReactorError(error, canister, method)`: it narrows `error.err` to that
method's `Err` arm after `kind === "canister_err"` (no cast), and it is `false`
for an error of any other method, canister object or `client.func` call (it
checks at run time). A failed write either certainly had no effect, or may
have executed:

| What happened                                                                   | `kind`                            | May have executed |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| refused before sending: arguments that do not encode (or an offered re-send's argument changed since: `arg_changed`), a write while signed out | `invalid_args`, `unauthenticated` | no |
| HTTP 4xx except 408 (429 included): the replica or a boundary node refused it    | `not_delivered`                   | no                |
| reject code 1, 2 (transient) or 3: rejected before any canister code ran         | `rejected` (2: `not_delivered`)   | no                |
| reject code 4 or 5: the canister rejected or trapped, maybe after changing state | `rejected`                        | yes (a write)     |
| a sent write got no trustworthy answer: network drop, timeout, 5xx, 408          | `outcome_unknown`                 | yes               |
| a reply that did not decode                                                      | `invalid_reply`                   | yes (a write)     |
| the canister returned `Err`                                                      | `canister_err`                    | no                |
| the caller changed, the call was aborted, an offered re-send would go elsewhere (`target_changed`), or a read's `timeoutMs` passed (`code: "timeout"`) | `cancelled` | no (an aborted write: yes) |

A write that got no answer (`outcome_unknown`, or `cancelled` with
`mayHaveExecuted: true`) carries `error.expiresAt`: the latest ingress expiry
its sends were signed with, a `bigint` of nanoseconds on the IC's clock
(about five minutes after the send). A `client.resendOf()` re-send whose
`timeoutMs` passed before it went out has none: the earlier error's
`expiresAt` still holds. Once the IC's time is past it, no send
of that write can still start running. For a method that commits without
awaiting another canister (an ICRC-1 transfer), a certified read-back of
state newer than that which finds nothing is final. Compare with a margin,
since the host's clock may differ from the IC's.

On the management canister (`aaaaa-aa`), codes 1 to 3 prove nothing: a write
there may have executed. A query changes nothing, so a failed read never "may
have executed".

How long a call waits: unless the call has a `timeoutMs` (below), neither the
client nor the agent puts a timeout on an HTTP request (the call or query, or a `read_state` that polls), so a request
that gets no answer waits as long as the `fetch` in use does. An accepted
update is polled for about five minutes (a deadline checked when a poll is
answered) before it rejects `outcome_unknown`. A read made with `queryOptions` stops
waiting at any point when TanStack Query cancels it
(`queryClient.cancelQueries(...)`, or its last observer unmounts), and
rejects `cancelled` (with `mayHaveExecuted: true` for an update read with
`{ update: "idempotent" }` whose request went out).

To bound the wait, give the canister target `timeoutMs`:
`client.canister<Actor>(actor, { id, timeoutMs: 15_000 })` bounds each of its
direct calls, `queryOptions` reads and mutations, counted from the call.
`client.mutationOptions(ledger, "icrc1_transfer", { timeoutMs: 15_000 })`
bounds that mutation's runs instead (1 to 2147483647 ms; anything else
throws). When it passes, the call stops waiting and rejects with
`code: "timeout"`: `cancelled`, `mayHaveExecuted: false`, for a read and for a
write that had not gone out; `outcome_unknown`, `mayHaveExecuted: true`, for a
write whose request went out, for an `{ update: "idempotent" }` read whose
request went out, and for a re-send of an offered write at any point. That
write may still execute: it is an unknown outcome to reconcile like any other
(read the state back, or `resendOf` for a method that deduplicates, given the
canister object the write went through: another `timeoutMs` is another
object), never one to send again blindly. Nothing is sent again for a
timeout, and the request is not torn down. Unlike other `cancelled` errors, a
`cancelled` with `code: "timeout"` is a real timeout: show it, do not ignore
it. Canister objects that differ only in `timeoutMs` share query keys, so a
read observed through two of them is bounded by the options TanStack Query
was given last.

## Outside React

```ts
import { principal } from "@candid-core/schema"
import { isReactorError, parseUnits } from "@ic-reactor/core"
import { client, ledger } from "./ledger"

const account = { owner: principal("aaaaa-aa"), subaccount: null }

const cached = await client.queryClient.fetchQuery(client.queryOptions(ledger, "icrc1_balance_of", account))
await client.queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: client.queryKey(ledger) })
const fresh = await ledger.icrc1_balance_of(account)

try {
  const arg = { to: account, amount: parseUnits("1.5", 8), fee: null, memo: null, from_subaccount: null, created_at_time: null }
  await ledger.icrc1_transfer(arg) // refused unless `client` was built with an Identity
} catch (error) {
  if (!isReactorError(error, ledger, "icrc1_transfer")) throw error
  if (error.kind === "canister_err") console.error(error.err.tag) // a TransferError
  else console.error(error.mayHaveExecuted ? "unknown outcome: re-read first" : error.kind)
}
```

Direct calls never touch a cache. To test, `createTestClient()` from
`@ic-reactor/core/testing` gives a real client over an in-memory replica with
a sign-in you control.

## Example

```tsx
import { principal } from "@candid-core/schema"
import { createClient } from "@ic-reactor/core"
import { ReactorProvider, useAuth, useClient } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { skipToken, useMutation, useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { toAuthLike, type SignInSource } from "./auth-like"
import { actor, type Actor } from "./generated/backend"

export function App({ auth }: { auth: SignInSource }) {
  return (
    <ReactorProvider client={() => createClient({ network: "ic", auth: () => toAuthLike(auth) })}>
      <Profile />
    </ReactorProvider>
  )
}

function Profile() {
  const client = useClient()
  const { status, principal: caller, signIn } = useAuth()
  const backend = client.canister<Actor>(actor, { id: "rrkah-fqaaa-aaaaa-aaaaq-cai" })
  const me = principal(caller)
  const signedIn = status === "signed-in"
  const profile = useQuery(client.queryOptions(backend, "get_profile", signedIn ? me : skipToken))
  const rename = useMutation(client.mutationOptions(backend, "set_name"))

  if (!signedIn) return <button onClick={() => void signIn()}>Sign in</button>
  if (profile.data === undefined) return <p>Loading…</p>
  return (
    <>
      <p>{profile.data.name}</p>
      <button disabled={rename.isPending} onClick={() => rename.mutate([me, "Ada"])}>Rename</button>
      {rename.error && <p>{rename.error.mayHaveExecuted ? "Unknown outcome" : rename.error.message}</p>}
    </>
  )
}
```

## Do not

- Cast text to `Principal`: use `principal(text)`.
- Convert `bigint` values to `number`: use `parseUnits` and `formatUnits`.
- Add `retry` to a write (`{ ...client.mutationOptions(...), retry: 3 }`
  compiles), or call a write from `useQuery`: TanStack Query may run a query's
  function again whenever it refetches, and every run of an update executes
  again.
- Write a query key by hand (it leaves the caller out), or carry data across
  keys (`keepPreviousData`, cross-key `initialData`).
- Build agents yourself, a client per render, or one client for every user of
  a server.
- Send a write as the anonymous identity: pass `identity: "anonymous"`, never
  an `AnonymousIdentity` you were handed.
- Treat every failed write as "not executed": read `mayHaveExecuted`.
